123	def _validate_structure(
124	    data: object,
125	) -> tuple[dict[str, dict[str, Any]], dict[str, str]]:
126	    if not isinstance(data, dict) or set(data.keys()) != set(_ROOT_FIELDS):
127	        raise ValueError("registry root must be an object with keys "
128	                         "version, jobs and idempotency")
129	
130	    version = data["version"]
131	    if not _is_plain_int(version) or version != _VERSION:
132	        raise ValueError("unsupported registry version")
133	
134	    jobs_raw = data["jobs"]
135	    idempotency_raw = data["idempotency"]
136	    if not isinstance(jobs_raw, dict) or not isinstance(idempotency_raw, dict):
137	        raise ValueError("jobs and idempotency must be objects")
138	
139	    jobs: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
140	    for name, record in jobs_raw.items():
141	        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name:
142	            raise ValueError("job ids must be non-empty strings")
143	        if not isinstance(record, dict) or set(record.keys()) != set(_JOB_FIELDS):
144	            raise ValueError("job record has invalid fields")
145	        if record["job_id"] != name:
146	            raise ValueError("job record id does not match its key")
147	        if not isinstance(record["job_id"], str):
148	            raise ValueError("job_id must be a string")
149	        if not _is_plain_int(record["deadline"]) or record["deadline"] < 0:
150	            raise ValueError("invalid deadline")
151	        if not _is_plain_int(record["energy_wh"]) or record["energy_wh"] <= 0:
152	            raise ValueError("invalid energy_wh")
153	        _validate_regions(record["residency_regions"])
154	        if record["state"] != _STATE:
155	            raise ValueError("invalid job state")
156	        jobs[name] = dict(record)
157	
158	    idempotency: dict[str, str] = {}
159	    referenced: set[str] = set()
160	    for key, job_id in idempotency_raw.items():
161	        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
162	            raise ValueError("idempotency keys must be non-empty strings")
163	        if not isinstance(job_id, str) or not job_id or job_id not in jobs:
164	            raise ValueError("idempotency entry must reference a registered job")
165	        if job_id in referenced:
166	            raise ValueError("job registered under more than one idempotency key")
167	        referenced.add(job_id)
168	        idempotency[key] = job_id
169	
170	    return jobs, idempotency

187	def _atomic_write(
188	    realpath: str,
189	    jobs: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
190	    idempotency: dict[str, str],
191	) -> None:
192	    payload = {
193	        "version": _VERSION,
194	        "jobs": {name: jobs[name] for name in sorted(jobs)},
195	        "idempotency": {key: idempotency[key] for key in sorted(idempotency)},
196	    }
197	    text = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"),
198	                      allow_nan=False) + "\n"
199	
200	    directory = os.path.dirname(realpath) or "."
201	    fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=directory, prefix=".jobs-", suffix=".tmp")
202	    try:
203	        with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as handle:
204	            handle.write(text)
205	            handle.flush()
206	            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
207	        os.replace(tmp_path, realpath)
208	    except BaseException:
209	        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
210	            os.unlink(tmp_path)
211	        raise
212	
213	    dir_fd = os.open(directory, os.O_RDONLY)
214	    try:
215	        os.fsync(dir_fd)
216	    finally:
217	        os.close(dir_fd)

220	def register(
221	    path: str,
222	    job: dict[str, object],
223	    idempotency_key: str,
224	) -> tuple[dict[str, object], bool]:
225	    """Register a job idempotently, persisting it as compact UTF-8 JSON.
226	
227	    Returns ``(record, created)`` where ``record`` carries job_id, deadline,
228	    energy_wh, residency_regions (sorted by code point) and ``state`` set to
229	    ``"queued"``; ``created`` is ``True`` for a new registration and ``False``
230	    when the idempotency key replays an identical, normalized job.
231	    """
232	    if not isinstance(path, str):
233	        raise ValueError("path must be a string")
234	    if not isinstance(idempotency_key, str) or not idempotency_key:
235	        raise ValueError("idempotency_key must be a non-empty string")
236	    job_id, deadline, energy_wh, regions = _normalize_job(job)
237	
238	    store = _get_store(path)
239	    with store.lock:
240	        jobs, idempotency = _load(store.realpath)
241	        record: dict[str, object] = {
242	            "job_id": job_id,
243	            "deadline": deadline,
244	            "energy_wh": energy_wh,
245	            "residency_regions": regions,
246	            "state": _STATE,
247	        }
248	
249	        existing_id = idempotency.get(idempotency_key)
250	        if existing_id is not None:
251	            existing = jobs[existing_id]
252	            if existing != record:
253	                raise ValueError("idempotency key was already used with a "
254	                                 "different job")
255	            return dict(existing), False
256	
257	        if job_id in jobs:
258	            raise ValueError("job_id is already registered under another "
259	                             "idempotency key")
260	
261	        jobs[job_id] = record
262	        idempotency[idempotency_key] = job_id
263	        _atomic_write(store.realpath, jobs, idempotency)
264	        return dict(record), True

272	@contextlib.contextmanager
273	def _process_lock(realpath: str, *, shared: bool = False) -> Iterator[None]:
274	    # The companion lock file is never unlinked; the kernel releases the
275	    # flock on process exit, so a leftover lock never blocks a later
276	    # call. Equivalent real paths in different processes therefore share
277	    # the same exclusive lock as the per-realpath in-process lock.
278	    lock_path = realpath + _LOCK_SUFFIX
279	    fd = os.open(lock_path, os.O_CREAT | os.O_RDWR, 0o666)
280	    try:
281	        fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_SH if shared else fcntl.LOCK_EX)
282	        try:
283	            yield
284	        finally:
285	            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
286	    finally:
287	        os.close(fd)

357	def _validate_submit_structure(data: object) -> tuple[
358	    dict[str, dict[str, Any]], dict[str, str], dict[str, dict[str, str]]
359	]:
360	    if not isinstance(data, dict) or set(data.keys()) != set(_SUBMIT_ROOT_FIELDS):
361	        raise ValueError("acceptance file root must be an object with keys "
362	                         "version, jobs, idempotency and audit")
363	
364	    version = data["version"]
365	    if not _is_plain_int(version) or version != _SUBMIT_VERSION:
366	        raise ValueError("unsupported acceptance file version")
367	
368	    jobs_raw = data["jobs"]
369	    idempotency_raw = data["idempotency"]
370	    audit_raw = data["audit"]
371	    if not isinstance(jobs_raw, dict) \
372	            or not isinstance(idempotency_raw, dict) \
373	            or not isinstance(audit_raw, dict):
374	        raise ValueError("jobs, idempotency and audit must be objects")
375	    _check_sorted_keys(jobs_raw, "jobs")
376	    _check_sorted_keys(idempotency_raw, "idempotency")
377	    _check_sorted_keys(audit_raw, "audit")
378	
379	    jobs: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
380	    for name, record in jobs_raw.items():
381	        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name:
382	            raise ValueError("job ids must be non-empty strings")
383	        if not isinstance(record, dict) \
384	                or set(record.keys()) != set(_SUBMIT_JOB_FIELDS):
385	            raise ValueError("job record has invalid fields")
386	        if record["job_id"] != name or not isinstance(record["job_id"], str):
387	            raise ValueError("job record id does not match its key")
388	        if not _is_plain_int(record["work"]) or record["work"] <= 0:
389	            raise ValueError("invalid work")
390	        for field in ("deadline", "max_cost", "carbon_cap"):
391	            if not _is_plain_int(record[field]) or record[field] < 0:
392	                raise ValueError(f"invalid {field}")
393	        regions = _validate_region_field(record["regions"], "regions")
394	        residency = _validate_region_field(record["residency"], "residency")
395	        if not set(residency).issubset(regions):
396	            raise ValueError("residency regions must be a subset of regions")
397	        if record["state"] != _STATE:
398	            raise ValueError("invalid job state")
399	        jobs[name] = {field: record[field] for field in _SUBMIT_JOB_FIELDS}
400	
401	    idempotency: dict[str, str] = {}
402	    referenced: set[str] = set()
403	    for key, job_id in idempotency_raw.items():
404	        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
405	            raise ValueError("idempotency keys must be non-empty strings")
406	        if not isinstance(job_id, str) or not job_id or job_id not in jobs:
407	            raise ValueError("idempotency entry must reference an accepted "
408	                             "job")
409	        if job_id in referenced:
410	            raise ValueError("job accepted under more than one idempotency "
411	                             "key")
412	        referenced.add(job_id)
413	        idempotency[key] = job_id
414	
415	    events: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = {}
416	    for key, event in audit_raw.items():
417	        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
418	            raise ValueError("audit keys must be non-empty strings")
419	        if not isinstance(event, dict) \
420	                or set(event.keys()) != set(_SUBMIT_EVENT_FIELDS):
421	            raise ValueError("submit audit event has invalid fields")
422	        event_key = event["key"]
423	        job_id = event["job_id"]
424	        result = event["result"]
425	        if event_key != key or not isinstance(event_key, str) or not event_key:
426	            raise ValueError("audit event key does not match its map key")
427	        if not isinstance(job_id, str) or not job_id or job_id not in jobs:
428	            raise ValueError("audit event must reference an accepted job")
429	        if result != _STATE:
430	            raise ValueError("audit event result must be queued")
431	        events[key] = {"key": event_key, "job_id": job_id,
432	                       "result": result}
433	
434	    # The three sections describe one acceptance history: each
435	    # idempotency key binds one job and one submit event, every accepted
436	    # job has both, and the event and the map agree on the job.
437	    if set(idempotency) != set(events):
438	        raise ValueError("idempotency keys and audit events do not match")
439	    for key, job_id in idempotency.items():
440	        if events[key]["job_id"] != job_id:
441	            raise ValueError("audit event does not match its idempotency "
442	                             "entry")
443	    if set(jobs) != referenced:
444	        raise ValueError("every accepted job must be bound to an "
445	                         "idempotency key")
446	
447	    return jobs, idempotency, events

493	def _rollback_submit_file(realpath: str, directory: str,
494	                          old_bytes: bytes | None,
495	                          first: BaseException) -> None:
496	    # Restore the exact pre-call bytes while the exclusive lock is held:
497	    # stage them back over the replaced file, or remove a file that did
498	    # not exist beforehand, then sync the directory. A failed recovery
499	    # surfaces chained after the original error.
500	    try:
501	        if old_bytes is None:
502	            try:
503	                os.unlink(realpath)
504	            except FileNotFoundError:
505	                pass
506	        else:
507	            fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
508	                dir=directory, prefix=".jobs-restore-", suffix=".tmp")
509	            try:
510	                with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
511	                    handle.write(old_bytes)
512	                    handle.flush()
513	                    os.fsync(handle.fileno())
514	                os.replace(tmp_path, realpath)
515	            except BaseException:
516	                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
517	                    os.unlink(tmp_path)
518	                raise
519	        _fsync_directory(directory)
520	    except OSError as recovery:
521	        raise recovery from first
522

524	def _fsync_directory(directory: str) -> None:
525	    dir_fd = os.open(directory, os.O_RDONLY)
526	    try:
527	        os.fsync(dir_fd)
528	    finally:
529	        os.close(dir_fd)

532	def _commit_submit_file(realpath: str, payload: bytes,
533	                        old_bytes: bytes | None) -> None:
534	    # One durable commit for jobs, the idempotency map and the audit
535	    # event: same-directory temporary, fsync, atomic replace and a
536	    # directory fsync. Any failure after the replace restores the
537	    # pre-call bytes, so an unsuccessful submit leaves the original file
538	    # byte-for-byte.
539	    directory = os.path.dirname(realpath) or "."
540	    fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
541	        dir=directory, prefix=".jobs-submit-", suffix=".tmp")
542	    try:
543	        with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
544	            handle.write(payload)
545	            handle.flush()
546	            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
547	        os.replace(tmp_path, realpath)
548	    except BaseException as first:
549	        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
550	            os.unlink(tmp_path)
551	        raise
552	    try:
553	        _fsync_directory(directory)
554	    except BaseException as first:
555	        _rollback_submit_file(realpath, directory, old_bytes, first)
556	        raise

559	def submit(path: str, job: dict[str, object], idempotency_key: str
560	           ) -> tuple[dict[str, object], bool]:
561	    """Persistently accept a complete scheduling-constraint job.
562	
563	    ``path`` and ``idempotency_key`` must be non-empty strings. The job
564	    must be an object with exactly the seven top-level fields job_id,
565	    work, deadline, regions, residency, max_cost and carbon_cap: a
566	    non-empty id, a positive work amount, non-negative deadline,
567	    max_cost and carbon_cap (booleans rejected), and two non-empty lists
568	    of distinct non-empty region strings, residency a subset of regions.
569	    Any deviation raises ``ValueError`` before the file is touched.
570	
571	    A first acceptance saves the canonical job -- both region lists
572	    sorted by code point, state ``"queued"`` -- together with the
573	    idempotency binding and a submit audit event carrying the key, the
574	    job id and the queued result, all three in one durable commit, and
575	    returns ``(record, True)``. Replaying the same key with an
576	    equivalent job returns the stored record with ``False`` without
577	    adding an event or rewriting the file; the same key with a different
578	    job, an already accepted job id under another key, or any constraint
579	    mismatch raises ``ValueError`` and preserves the original bytes.
580	
581	    A missing parent directory raises ``FileNotFoundError``; an invalid
582	    existing file (encoding, JSON, negative-zero or non-finite numbers,
583	    version, structure, ordering or references) raises ``ValueError``;
584	    any other locking or I/O failure raises ``OSError``. Calls serialize
585	    across threads and processes per resolved real path.
586	    """
587	    if not isinstance(path, str) or not path:
588	        raise ValueError("path must be a non-empty string")
589	    if not isinstance(idempotency_key, str) or not idempotency_key:
590	        raise ValueError("idempotency_key must be a non-empty string")
591	    record = _normalize_submit_job(job)
592	    job_id = record["job_id"]
593	
594	    store = _get_store(path)

634	    ``ValueError``; an unknown job id raises ``KeyError(job_id)``; any
635	    other locking or I/O failure raises ``OSError``. The call never
636	    writes, and the returned record is a fresh copy with job_id, work,
637	    deadline, regions, residency, max_cost, carbon_cap and state.
638	    """
639	    if not isinstance(path, str) or not path:
640	        raise ValueError("path must be a non-empty string")

642	        raise ValueError("job_id must be a non-empty string")

646	        jobs, _idempotency, _events, raw = _load_submit_file(realpath)

368	    if not (resource["start"] <= at <= resource["end"]):
369	        raise ValueError("trade candidate must be valid at the trade's "
370	                         "evaluation moment")
371	    # Static trades price on the version's baked-in figures; live trades
372	    # price on the frozen signal for the same region.
373	    if live:
374	        unit_cost, carbon_intensity = _validate_signal(
375	            entry["signal"], resource["region"], at, signal_history)
376	    else:
377	        unit_cost = resource["unit_cost"]
378	        carbon_intensity = resource["carbon_intensity"]
379	    total_cost = entry["total_cost"]
380	    total_carbon = entry["total_carbon"]
381	    if not _is_plain_int(total_cost) or total_cost < 0 \
382	            or total_cost != work * unit_cost:
383	        raise ValueError("trade candidate total_cost is invalid")
384	    if not _is_plain_int(total_carbon) or total_carbon < 0 \
385	            or total_carbon != work * carbon_intensity:
386	        raise ValueError("trade candidate total_carbon is invalid")
387	    # The snapshot must still describe the same feasibility the trade
388	    # was decided under; published versions and accepted jobs never
389	    # change, so a valid trade stays valid forever.
390	    if resource["region"] not in set(job["regions"]):
391	        raise ValueError("trade candidate is outside the job's regions")
392	    if not set(job["residency"]) <= set(resource["residency"]):
393	        raise ValueError("trade candidate does not cover job residency")
394	    if resource["end"] < job["deadline"]:
395	        raise ValueError("trade candidate does not cover the job deadline")
396	    if total_cost > job["max_cost"] \
397	            or total_carbon > job["carbon_cap"]:
398	        raise ValueError("trade candidate exceeds a job budget")
399	    return live, carbon_intensity, unit_cost, resource_id

402	def _validate_trade(
403	    record: object,
404	    accepted: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
405	    history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]],
406	    signal_history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]] | None,
407	) -> dict[str, Any]:
408	    if not isinstance(record, dict) \
409	            or set(record.keys()) != set(_TRADE_FIELDS):
410	        raise ValueError("trade record has invalid fields")
411	    job_id = record["job_id"]
412	    at = record["at"]
413	    work = record["work"]
414	    resource_id = record["resource_id"]
415	    version = record["version"]
416	    if not isinstance(job_id, str) or not job_id:
417	        raise ValueError("trade job_id must be a non-empty string")
418	    if not _is_plain_int(at) or at < 0:
419	        raise ValueError("trade at must be a non-boolean non-negative "
420	                         "integer")
421	    if not _is_plain_int(work) or work <= 0:
422	        raise ValueError("trade work must be a positive integer")
423	    if not isinstance(resource_id, str) or not resource_id:
424	        raise ValueError("trade resource_id must be a non-empty string")
425	    if not _is_plain_int(version) or version < 1:
426	        raise ValueError("trade version must be a positive integer")
427	    selection = record["selection"]
428	    if not isinstance(selection, dict) \
429	            or set(selection.keys()) != set(_SELECTION_FIELDS):
430	        raise ValueError("trade selection has invalid fields")
431	    if selection["resource_id"] != resource_id \
432	            or not isinstance(selection["resource_id"], str):
433	        raise ValueError("trade selection does not name its resource")
434	    if selection["version"] != version:
435	        raise ValueError("trade selection does not name its version")
436	
437	    job = accepted.get(job_id)
438	    if job is None:
439	        raise ValueError("trade must reference an accepted job")
440	    if work != job["work"]:
441	        raise ValueError("trade work does not match its accepted job")
442	    records = history.get(resource_id)
443	    if records is None or version > len(records):
444	        raise ValueError("trade must reference a published resource version")
445	
446	    candidates_raw = record["candidates"]
447	    if not isinstance(candidates_raw, list) or not candidates_raw:
448	        raise ValueError("trade candidates must be a non-empty list")
449	    candidates: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
450	    last_rank: tuple[int, int, str] | None = None
451	    seen: set[str] = set()
452	    live_kind: bool | None = None
453	    for entry_raw in candidates_raw:
454	        live, carbon, unit_cost, candidate_id = _validate_candidate(
455	            entry_raw, work, at, job, history, signal_history, seen)
456	        # A trade is decided under exactly one pricing mode: static
457	        # trades never carry a signal, live trades always carry one.
458	        if live_kind is None:
459	            live_kind = live
460	        elif live != live_kind:
461	            raise ValueError("trade candidates must all be static or all "
462	                             "live")
463	        rank = (carbon, unit_cost, candidate_id)
464	        if last_rank is not None and rank < last_rank:
465	            raise ValueError("trade candidates must be ordered by carbon "
466	                             "intensity, unit cost and resource id")
467	        last_rank = rank
468	        # Keep the parsed key order: the candidate's resource must equal
469	        # the supply record field-for-field and its frozen signal -- when
470	        # resolvable -- the published signal, while the ledger's
471	        # canonical-byte comparison rejects any reordered nested object.
472	        candidates.append(copy.deepcopy(entry_raw))
473	
474	    # The first ordered candidate is the unique winner.
475	    winner = candidates[0]["resource"]
476	    if winner["resource_id"] != resource_id or winner["version"] != version:
477	        raise ValueError("trade selection must be the first ordered "
478	                         "candidate")
479	    return {
480	        "job_id": job_id,
481	        "at": at,
482	        "work": work,
483	        "resource_id": resource_id,
484	        "version": version,
485	        "candidates": candidates,
486	        "selection": {"resource_id": resource_id, "version": version},
487	    }

490	def _validate_clear_ledger(
491	    data: object,
492	    accepted: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
493	    history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]],
494	    signal_history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]] | None = None,
495	) -> tuple[dict[str, dict[str, Any]], dict[str, dict[str, Any]]]:
496	    if not isinstance(data, dict) or set(data.keys()) != set(_CLEAR_ROOT_FIELDS):
497	        raise ValueError("clearing ledger root must be an object with keys "
498	                         "version, trades, idempotency and audit")
499	    version = data["version"]
500	    if not _is_plain_int(version) or version != _CLEAR_VERSION:
501	        raise ValueError("unsupported clearing ledger version")
502	
503	    trades_raw = data["trades"]
504	    idempotency_raw = data["idempotency"]
505	    audit_raw = data["audit"]
506	    if not isinstance(trades_raw, dict) \
507	            or not isinstance(idempotency_raw, dict) \
508	            or not isinstance(audit_raw, dict):
509	        raise ValueError("trades, idempotency and audit must be objects")
510	    _check_sorted_keys(trades_raw, "trades")
511	    _check_sorted_keys(idempotency_raw, "idempotency")
512	    _check_sorted_keys(audit_raw, "audit")
513	
514	    trades: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
515	    for job_id, record in trades_raw.items():
516	        if not isinstance(job_id, str) or not job_id:
517	            raise ValueError("trade job ids must be non-empty strings")
518	        trade = _validate_trade(record, accepted, history, signal_history)
519	        if trade["job_id"] != job_id:
520	            raise ValueError("trade record id does not match its key")
521	        trades[job_id] = trade
522	
523	    idempotency: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
524	    events: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
525	    referenced: set[str] = set()
526	    for key, binding in idempotency_raw.items():
527	        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
528	            raise ValueError("idempotency keys must be non-empty strings")
529	        if not isinstance(binding, dict) \
530	                or set(binding.keys()) != {"job_id", "at"}:
531	            raise ValueError("idempotency binding has invalid fields")
532	        bound_job = binding["job_id"]
533	        bound_at = binding["at"]
534	        if not isinstance(bound_job, str) or not bound_job \
535	                or bound_job not in trades:
536	            raise ValueError("idempotency entry must reference a recorded "
537	                             "trade")
538	        if not _is_plain_int(bound_at) or bound_at < 0:
539	            raise ValueError("idempotency entry must bind an evaluation "
540	                             "moment")
541	        if bound_job in referenced:
542	            raise ValueError("job traded under more than one idempotency "
543	                             "key")
544	        referenced.add(bound_job)
545	        trade = trades[bound_job]
546	        if trade["at"] != bound_at:
547	            raise ValueError("idempotency entry does not match its trade")
548	        idempotency[key] = {"job_id": bound_job, "at": bound_at}
549	
550	    for key, event in audit_raw.items():
551	        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
552	            raise ValueError("audit keys must be non-empty strings")
553	        if not isinstance(event, dict) \
554	                or set(event.keys()) != set(_EVENT_FIELDS):
555	            raise ValueError("clear audit event has invalid fields")
556	        event_key = event["key"]
557	        job_id = event["job_id"]
558	        at = event["at"]
559	        resource_id = event["resource_id"]
560	        event_version = event["version"]
561	        if event_key != key or not isinstance(event_key, str) or not event_key:
562	            raise ValueError("audit event key does not match its map key")
563	        if not isinstance(job_id, str) or not job_id or job_id not in trades:
564	            raise ValueError("audit event must reference a recorded trade")
565	        if not _is_plain_int(at) or at < 0:
566	            raise ValueError("audit event at must be a non-negative integer")
567	        if not isinstance(resource_id, str) or not resource_id:
568	            raise ValueError("audit event resource_id must be a non-empty "
569	                             "string")
570	        if not _is_plain_int(event_version) or event_version < 1:
571	            raise ValueError("audit event version must be a positive integer")
572	        trade = trades[job_id]
573	        if at != trade["at"] or resource_id != trade["resource_id"] \
574	                or event_version != trade["version"]:
575	            raise ValueError("audit event does not match its trade")
576	        events[key] = {"key": event_key, "job_id": job_id, "at": at,
577	                       "resource_id": resource_id, "version": event_version}
578	
579	    # The three sections describe one clearing history: each idempotency
580	    # key binds one trade and one event, and each trade is bound exactly
581	    # once.
582	    if set(idempotency) != set(events):
583	        raise ValueError("idempotency keys and audit events do not match")
584	    for key, binding in idempotency.items():
585	        event = events[key]
586	        if event["job_id"] != binding["job_id"] or event["at"] != binding["at"]:
587	            raise ValueError("audit event does not match its idempotency "
588	                             "entry")
589	    if set(trades) != referenced:
590	        raise ValueError("every trade must be bound to an idempotency key")
591	
592	    # Recorded bookings may not oversell any published version; every
593	    # winner was feasible with the earlier trades' work deducted.
594	    booked: dict[tuple[str, int], int] = {}
595	    for trade in trades.values():
596	        slot = (trade["resource_id"], trade["version"])
597	        booked[slot] = booked.get(slot, 0) + trade["work"]
598	    for (resource_id, version), amount in booked.items():
599	        record = history[resource_id][version - 1]
600	        if record["capacity"] < amount:
601	            raise ValueError("ledger oversells a published resource version")
602	
603	    return trades, idempotency

606	def _canonical_clear_bytes(
607	    trades: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
608	    idempotency: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
609	) -> bytes:
610	    audit = {key: {
611	        "key": key,
612	        "job_id": trades[binding["job_id"]]["job_id"],
613	        "at": binding["at"],
614	        "resource_id": trades[binding["job_id"]]["resource_id"],
615	        "version": trades[binding["job_id"]]["version"],
616	    } for key, binding in idempotency.items()}
617	    payload = {
618	        "version": _CLEAR_VERSION,
619	        "trades": {job_id: trades[job_id] for job_id in sorted(trades)},
620	        "idempotency": {key: idempotency[key] for key in sorted(idempotency)},
621	        "audit": {key: audit[key] for key in sorted(audit)},
622	    }
623	    text = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"),
624	                      allow_nan=False) + "\n"
625	    return text.encode("utf-8")

629	    realpath: str,
630	    accepted: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
631	    history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]],
632	    signal_history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]] | None = None,
633	) -> tuple[dict[str, dict[str, Any]], dict[str, dict[str, Any]], bytes | None]:
634	    try:

636	            raw = handle.read()

642	        raise ValueError(
643	            f"clearing ledger {realpath!r} is not valid UTF-8") from exc
644	    try:
645	        # Negative-zero and non-finite literals are format errors.
646	        data = finite_loads(text)
647	    except ValueError as exc:
648	        raise ValueError(
649	            f"clearing ledger {realpath!r} is not valid JSON") from exc

654	    if raw != _canonical_clear_bytes(trades, idempotency):
655	        raise ValueError(
656	            f"clearing ledger {realpath!r} is not in canonical compact form")

717	    except BaseException as first:

_CLEAR_VERSION = 2
_CLEAR_ROOT_FIELDS = ("version", "trades", "idempotency", "audit")
_TRADE_FIELDS = ("job_id", "at", "work", "resource_id", "version",
                 "candidates", "selection")
_SELECTION_FIELDS = ("resource_id", "version")
_EVENT_FIELDS = ("key", "job_id", "at", "resource_id", "version")
_STATIC_CANDIDATE_FIELDS = ("resource", "total_cost", "total_carbon")
_LIVE_CANDIDATE_FIELDS = ("resource", "signal", "total_cost",
                          "total_carbon")
_LOCK_SUFFIX = ".lock"


@contextlib.contextmanager
def _clear_lock(realpath: str, *, shared: bool = False) -> Iterator[None]:
    # As in resources.jobs, the companion lock file is never unlinked and
    # an flock is released by the kernel on process exit, so equivalent
    # real paths share one lock across threads and processes.
    lock_path = realpath + _LOCK_SUFFIX
    fd = os.open(lock_path, os.O_CREAT | os.O_RDWR, 0o666)
    try:
        fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_SH if shared else fcntl.LOCK_EX)
        try:
            yield
        finally:
            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
    finally:
        os.close(fd)


def _check_sorted_keys(mapping: dict[Any, Any], label: str) -> None:
    keys = list(mapping)
    if keys != sorted(keys):
        raise ValueError(f"{label} must be ordered by key code point")


def _validate_signal(
    signal: object,
    resource_region: str,
    at: int,
    signal_history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]] | None,
) -> tuple[int, int]:
    # Returns the binary numeric pair (unit_cost, carbon_intensity) the
    # caller prices on, never the signal record itself. A live candidate
    # freezes the exact published signal record -- region, version and
    # all observations -- so a later signal publish cannot change what an
    # earlier trade was decided under. When the
    # signal snapshot is available (clear_live), the frozen record must
    # be the exact published version. Readers that never take the signal
    # file (static clear, dispatch, execution) still validate the frozen
    # record structurally and arithmetically: its totals, window and
    # budget relations are all decidable from the frozen bytes, so their
    # invariants hold without resolving the reference.
    if not isinstance(signal, dict) \
            or set(signal.keys()) != set(_signals._RECORD_FIELDS):
        raise ValueError("trade candidate signal has invalid fields")
    region = signal["region"]
    version = signal["version"]
    if region != resource_region:
        raise ValueError("trade candidate signal must cover the resource "
                         "region")
    if not _is_plain_int(version) or version < 1:
        raise ValueError("candidate signal version must be a positive "
                         "integer")
    # Validate a copy: _check_values normalizes the mix order in place,
    # and the parsed record's raw key order must be left untouched so the
    # ledger's canonical-byte comparison still rejects a reordered mix.
    signal_copy = dict(signal)
    signal_copy["mix"] = dict(signal["mix"])
    _signals._check_values(signal_copy)
    if signal_history is not None:
        records = signal_history.get(region)
        if records is None or version > len(records) \
                or dict(signal) != records[version - 1]:
            raise ValueError("trade candidate signal must reference a "
                             "published signal version")
    if not (signal["observed"] <= at <= signal["expires"]):
        raise ValueError("trade candidate signal must be valid at the "
                         "trade's evaluation moment")
    return signal["unit_cost"], signal["carbon_intensity"]


def _validate_candidate(
    entry: object,
    work: int,
    at: int,
    job: dict[str, Any],
    history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]],
    signal_history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]] | None,
    seen: set[str],
) -> tuple[bool, int, int, str]:
    if not isinstance(entry, dict) \
            or set(entry.keys()) not in (set(_STATIC_CANDIDATE_FIELDS),
                                         set(_LIVE_CANDIDATE_FIELDS)):
        raise ValueError("trade candidate has invalid fields")
    live = "signal" in entry
    resource = entry["resource"]
    if not isinstance(resource, dict) \
            or set(resource.keys()) != set(_resources._RECORD_FIELDS):
        raise ValueError("trade candidate resource has invalid fields")
    # Strict value typing (booleans rejected), the same rules a
    # published version had to satisfy.
    _resources._check_values(resource)
    resource_id = resource["resource_id"]
    version = resource["version"]
    if not isinstance(resource_id, str) or not resource_id:
        raise ValueError("candidate resource_id must be a non-empty string")
    if not _is_plain_int(version) or version < 1:
        raise ValueError("candidate version must be a positive integer")
    # The versioned record must be the exact, immutable supply record.
    records = history.get(resource_id)
    if records is None or version > len(records) \
            or dict(resource) != records[version - 1]:
        raise ValueError("trade candidate must reference a published "
                         "resource version")
    if resource_id in seen:
        raise ValueError("trade candidates must be distinct resources")
    seen.add(resource_id)
    if not (resource["start"] <= at <= resource["end"]):
        raise ValueError("trade candidate must be valid at the trade's "
                         "evaluation moment")
    # Static trades price on the version's baked-in figures; live trades
    # price on the frozen signal for the same region.
    if live:
        unit_cost, carbon_intensity = _validate_signal(
            entry["signal"], resource["region"], at, signal_history)
    else:
        unit_cost = resource["unit_cost"]
        carbon_intensity = resource["carbon_intensity"]
    total_cost = entry["total_cost"]
    total_carbon = entry["total_carbon"]
    if not _is_plain_int(total_cost) or total_cost < 0 \
            or total_cost != work * unit_cost:
        raise ValueError("trade candidate total_cost is invalid")
    if not _is_plain_int(total_carbon) or total_carbon < 0 \
            or total_carbon != work * carbon_intensity:
        raise ValueError("trade candidate total_carbon is invalid")
    # The snapshot must still describe the same feasibility the trade
    # was decided under; published versions and accepted jobs never
    # change, so a valid trade stays valid forever.
    if resource["region"] not in set(job["regions"]):
        raise ValueError("trade candidate is outside the job's regions")
    if not set(job["residency"]) <= set(resource["residency"]):
        raise ValueError("trade candidate does not cover job residency")
    if resource["end"] < job["deadline"]:
        raise ValueError("trade candidate does not cover the job deadline")
    if total_cost > job["max_cost"] \
            or total_carbon > job["carbon_cap"]:
        raise ValueError("trade candidate exceeds a job budget")
    return live, carbon_intensity, unit_cost, resource_id


def _validate_trade(
    record: object,
    accepted: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
    history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]],
    signal_history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]] | None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    if not isinstance(record, dict) \
            or set(record.keys()) != set(_TRADE_FIELDS):
        raise ValueError("trade record has invalid fields")
    job_id = record["job_id"]
    at = record["at"]
    work = record["work"]
    resource_id = record["resource_id"]
    version = record["version"]
    if not isinstance(job_id, str) or not job_id:
        raise ValueError("trade job_id must be a non-empty string")
    if not _is_plain_int(at) or at < 0:
        raise ValueError("trade at must be a non-boolean non-negative "
                         "integer")
    if not _is_plain_int(work) or work <= 0:
        raise ValueError("trade work must be a positive integer")
    if not isinstance(resource_id, str) or not resource_id:
        raise ValueError("trade resource_id must be a non-empty string")
    if not _is_plain_int(version) or version < 1:
        raise ValueError("trade version must be a positive integer")
    selection = record["selection"]
    if not isinstance(selection, dict) \
            or set(selection.keys()) != set(_SELECTION_FIELDS):
        raise ValueError("trade selection has invalid fields")
    if selection["resource_id"] != resource_id \
            or not isinstance(selection["resource_id"], str):
        raise ValueError("trade selection does not name its resource")
    if selection["version"] != version:
        raise ValueError("trade selection does not name its version")

    job = accepted.get(job_id)
    if job is None:
        raise ValueError("trade must reference an accepted job")
    if work != job["work"]:
        raise ValueError("trade work does not match its accepted job")
    records = history.get(resource_id)
    if records is None or version > len(records):
        raise ValueError("trade must reference a published resource version")

    candidates_raw = record["candidates"]
    if not isinstance(candidates_raw, list) or not candidates_raw:
        raise ValueError("trade candidates must be a non-empty list")
    candidates: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    last_rank: tuple[int, int, str] | None = None
    seen: set[str] = set()
    live_kind: bool | None = None
    for entry_raw in candidates_raw:
        live, carbon, unit_cost, candidate_id = _validate_candidate(
            entry_raw, work, at, job, history, signal_history, seen)
        # A trade is decided under exactly one pricing mode: static
        # trades never carry a signal, live trades always carry one.
        if live_kind is None:
            live_kind = live
        elif live != live_kind:
            raise ValueError("trade candidates must all be static or all "
                             "live")
        rank = (carbon, unit_cost, candidate_id)
        if last_rank is not None and rank < last_rank:
            raise ValueError("trade candidates must be ordered by carbon "
                             "intensity, unit cost and resource id")
        last_rank = rank
        # Keep the parsed key order: the candidate's resource must equal
        # the supply record field-for-field and its frozen signal -- when
        # resolvable -- the published signal, while the ledger's
        # canonical-byte comparison rejects any reordered nested object.
        candidates.append(copy.deepcopy(entry_raw))

    # The first ordered candidate is the unique winner.
    winner = candidates[0]["resource"]
    if winner["resource_id"] != resource_id or winner["version"] != version:
        raise ValueError("trade selection must be the first ordered "
                         "candidate")
    return {
        "job_id": job_id,
        "at": at,
        "work": work,
        "resource_id": resource_id,
        "version": version,
        "candidates": candidates,
        "selection": {"resource_id": resource_id, "version": version},
    }


def _validate_clear_ledger(
    data: object,
    accepted: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
    history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]],
    signal_history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]] | None = None,
) -> tuple[dict[str, dict[str, Any]], dict[str, dict[str, Any]]]:
    if not isinstance(data, dict) or set(data.keys()) != set(_CLEAR_ROOT_FIELDS):
        raise ValueError("clearing ledger root must be an object with keys "
                         "version, trades, idempotency and audit")
    version = data["version"]
    if not _is_plain_int(version) or version != _CLEAR_VERSION:
        raise ValueError("unsupported clearing ledger version")

    trades_raw = data["trades"]
    idempotency_raw = data["idempotency"]
    audit_raw = data["audit"]
    if not isinstance(trades_raw, dict) \
            or not isinstance(idempotency_raw, dict) \
            or not isinstance(audit_raw, dict):
        raise ValueError("trades, idempotency and audit must be objects")
    _check_sorted_keys(trades_raw, "trades")
    _check_sorted_keys(idempotency_raw, "idempotency")
    _check_sorted_keys(audit_raw, "audit")

    trades: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
    for job_id, record in trades_raw.items():
        if not isinstance(job_id, str) or not job_id:
            raise ValueError("trade job ids must be non-empty strings")
        trade = _validate_trade(record, accepted, history, signal_history)
        if trade["job_id"] != job_id:
            raise ValueError("trade record id does not match its key")
        trades[job_id] = trade

    idempotency: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
    events: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
    referenced: set[str] = set()
    for key, binding in idempotency_raw.items():
        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
            raise ValueError("idempotency keys must be non-empty strings")
        if not isinstance(binding, dict) \
                or set(binding.keys()) != {"job_id", "at"}:
            raise ValueError("idempotency binding has invalid fields")
        bound_job = binding["job_id"]
        bound_at = binding["at"]
        if not isinstance(bound_job, str) or not bound_job \
                or bound_job not in trades:
            raise ValueError("idempotency entry must reference a recorded "
                             "trade")
        if not _is_plain_int(bound_at) or bound_at < 0:
            raise ValueError("idempotency entry must bind an evaluation "
                             "moment")
        if bound_job in referenced:
            raise ValueError("job traded under more than one idempotency "
                             "key")
        referenced.add(bound_job)
        trade = trades[bound_job]
        if trade["at"] != bound_at:
            raise ValueError("idempotency entry does not match its trade")
        idempotency[key] = {"job_id": bound_job, "at": bound_at}

    for key, event in audit_raw.items():
        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
            raise ValueError("audit keys must be non-empty strings")
        if not isinstance(event, dict) \
                or set(event.keys()) != set(_EVENT_FIELDS):
            raise ValueError("clear audit event has invalid fields")
        event_key = event["key"]
        job_id = event["job_id"]
        at = event["at"]
        resource_id = event["resource_id"]
        event_version = event["version"]
        if event_key != key or not isinstance(event_key, str) or not event_key:
            raise ValueError("audit event key does not match its map key")
        if not isinstance(job_id, str) or not job_id or job_id not in trades:
            raise ValueError("audit event must reference a recorded trade")
        if not _is_plain_int(at) or at < 0:
            raise ValueError("audit event at must be a non-negative integer")
        if not isinstance(resource_id, str) or not resource_id:
            raise ValueError("audit event resource_id must be a non-empty "
                             "string")
        if not _is_plain_int(event_version) or event_version < 1:
            raise ValueError("audit event version must be a positive integer")
        trade = trades[job_id]
        if at != trade["at"] or resource_id != trade["resource_id"] \
                or event_version != trade["version"]:
            raise ValueError("audit event does not match its trade")
        events[key] = {"key": event_key, "job_id": job_id, "at": at,
                       "resource_id": resource_id, "version": event_version}

    # The three sections describe one clearing history: each idempotency
    # key binds one trade and one event, and each trade is bound exactly
    # once.
    if set(idempotency) != set(events):
        raise ValueError("idempotency keys and audit events do not match")
    for key, binding in idempotency.items():
        event = events[key]
        if event["job_id"] != binding["job_id"] or event["at"] != binding["at"]:
            raise ValueError("audit event does not match its idempotency "
                             "entry")
    if set(trades) != referenced:
        raise ValueError("every trade must be bound to an idempotency key")

    # Recorded bookings may not oversell any published version; every
    # winner was feasible with the earlier trades' work deducted.
    booked: dict[tuple[str, int], int] = {}
    for trade in trades.values():
        slot = (trade["resource_id"], trade["version"])
        booked[slot] = booked.get(slot, 0) + trade["work"]
    for (resource_id, version), amount in booked.items():
        record = history[resource_id][version - 1]
        if record["capacity"] < amount:
            raise ValueError("ledger oversells a published resource version")

    return trades, idempotency


def _canonical_clear_bytes(
    trades: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
    idempotency: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
) -> bytes:
    audit = {key: {
        "key": key,
        "job_id": trades[binding["job_id"]]["job_id"],
        "at": binding["at"],
        "resource_id": trades[binding["job_id"]]["resource_id"],
        "version": trades[binding["job_id"]]["version"],
    } for key, binding in idempotency.items()}
    payload = {
        "version": _CLEAR_VERSION,
        "trades": {job_id: trades[job_id] for job_id in sorted(trades)},
        "idempotency": {key: idempotency[key] for key in sorted(idempotency)},
        "audit": {key: audit[key] for key in sorted(audit)},
    }
    text = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"),
                      allow_nan=False) + "\n"
    return text.encode("utf-8")


def _load_clear_ledger(
    realpath: str,
    accepted: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
    history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]],
    signal_history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]] | None = None,
) -> tuple[dict[str, dict[str, Any]], dict[str, dict[str, Any]], bytes | None]:
    try:
        with open(realpath, "rb") as handle:
            raw = handle.read()
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return {}, {}, None
    try:
        text = raw.decode("utf-8")
    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
        raise ValueError(
            f"clearing ledger {realpath!r} is not valid UTF-8") from exc
    try:
        # Negative-zero and non-finite literals are format errors.
        data = finite_loads(text)
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise ValueError(
            f"clearing ledger {realpath!r} is not valid JSON") from exc
    trades, idempotency = _validate_clear_ledger(
        data, accepted, history, signal_history)
    # As for the supply file, the ledger is accepted only in canonical
    # compact form with a single trailing newline.
    if raw != _canonical_clear_bytes(trades, idempotency):
        raise ValueError(
            f"clearing ledger {realpath!r} is not in canonical compact form")
    return trades, idempotency, raw


def _fsync_directory(directory: str) -> None:
    dir_fd = os.open(directory, os.O_RDONLY)
    try:
        os.fsync(dir_fd)
    finally:
        os.close(dir_fd)


def _rollback_clear(realpath: str, directory: str, old_bytes: bytes | None,
                    first: BaseException) -> None:
    # Restore the exact pre-call bytes while the exclusive lock is held,
    # or remove a ledger that did not exist beforehand, then sync the
    # directory. A failed recovery chains after the original error.
    try:
        if old_bytes is None:
            try:
                os.unlink(realpath)
            except FileNotFoundError:
                pass
        else:
            fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
                dir=directory, prefix=".clear-restore-", suffix=".tmp")
            try:
                with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
                    handle.write(old_bytes)
                    handle.flush()
                    os.fsync(handle.fileno())
                os.replace(tmp_path, realpath)
            except BaseException:
                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
                    os.unlink(tmp_path)
                raise
        _fsync_directory(directory)
    except OSError as recovery:
        raise recovery from first


def _commit_clear(realpath: str, payload: bytes,
                  old_bytes: bytes | None) -> None:
    # One durable commit for the trade, the idempotency binding and the
    # audit event: synced same-directory temporary, atomic replace and a
    # directory fsync, restoring the pre-call bytes on any failure.
    directory = os.path.dirname(realpath) or "."
    fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
        dir=directory, prefix=".clear-", suffix=".tmp")
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
            handle.write(payload)
            handle.flush()
            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
        os.replace(tmp_path, realpath)
    except BaseException:
        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
            os.unlink(tmp_path)
        raise
    try:
        _fsync_directory(directory)
    except BaseException as first:
        _rollback_clear(realpath, directory, old_bytes, first)
        raise

def clear_live(
    jobs: str,
    supply: str,
    signals: str,
    ledger: str,
    job_id: str,
    key: str,
    at: int,
) -> tuple[dict[str, object], bool]:
    """Clear one accepted job against live signals idempotently.

    This is the dynamic counterpart of :func:`clear` and shares the same
    clearing ledger: trades booked by either call deduct capacity from
    the same resource versions. ``jobs``, ``supply``, ``signals`` and
    ``ledger`` paths, ``job_id`` and ``key`` must be non-empty strings
    and ``at`` a non-boolean non-negative integer evaluation moment;
    the four paths must also resolve to distinct real locations. Any
    violation raises ``ValueError`` before a business file is read.

    The acceptance file, the supply file and the live signal file are
    read as one snapshot under their shared locks together with the
    ledger's exclusive lock, all four taken in resolved real-path
    order. Only each resource's highest supply version valid at ``at``
    is considered, and region, residency, budget, deadline and capacity
    already booked against the exact resource version -- by a static
    :func:`clear` trade or a live one -- follow :func:`clear`. The unit
    cost and carbon intensity, however, come from the resource region's
    latest signal observed no later than ``at`` and not expired at it;
    a region without such a signal contributes no candidate. Remaining
    candidates are ordered by signal carbon intensity, signal unit cost
    and resource id; the first one is the unique winner.

    Returns ``(trade, created)``. The trade freezes the ordered
    candidates with both their immutable resource version and their
    immutable signal version (the selection keeps resource id and
    version), so a signal published afterwards can never change an
    earlier trade. A missing ledger is created only on the first trade;
    the trade, the idempotency binding (key to job id and evaluation
    moment) and the audit event are committed together in one synced
    atomic write, byte-compatible with :func:`clear`. Replaying the same
    key with the same job and evaluation moment returns the stored
    trade -- static or live -- with ``False`` without reselecting,
    appending an event or rewriting a byte. The same key with a changed
    request, or a job already traded under another idempotency key,
    raises ``ValueError`` and leaves the ledger byte-for-byte untouched.

    An unknown job raises ``KeyError`` and no remaining feasible
    resource raises ``LookupError``; neither creates the ledger. Missing
    input files or a missing ledger parent raise ``FileNotFoundError``
    without leaving a ledger or temporary fragment. Invalid structure,
    references, ordering or non-canonical bytes raise ``ValueError``;
    other locking, read/write or sync failures raise ``OSError``. The
    existing :func:`match`, :func:`clear`, the ``resources`` interfaces,
    serving and HTTP behavior are unchanged.
    """
    for value in (jobs, supply, signals, ledger, job_id, key):
        if not isinstance(value, str) or not value:
            raise ValueError("jobs, supply, signals, ledger, job_id and key "
                             "must be non-empty strings")
    if not _is_plain_int(at) or at < 0:
        raise ValueError("at must be a non-boolean non-negative integer")

    job_real = os.path.realpath(jobs)
    supply_real = os.path.realpath(supply)
    signal_real = os.path.realpath(signals)
    ledger_real = os.path.realpath(ledger)
    if len({job_real, supply_real, signal_real, ledger_real}) != 4:
        raise ValueError("jobs, supply, signals and ledger paths must be "
                         "distinct real paths")

    store = _get_store(ledger)
    with store.lock:
        # Locks are taken in one resolved-real-path order shared by
        # every caller, so concurrent clears can never deadlock; the
        # ledger lock is exclusive, all three snapshots shared.
        with contextlib.ExitStack() as stack:
            for locked in sorted({job_real, supply_real, signal_real,
                                  ledger_real}):
                stack.enter_context(
                    _clear_lock(locked, shared=(locked != ledger_real)))

            accepted, job_map, job_events, job_raw = \
                _jobs._load_submit_file(job_real)
            if job_raw is None:
                raise FileNotFoundError(
                    f"acceptance file {job_real!r} does not exist")
            if job_raw != _jobs._serialize_submit_file(
                    accepted, job_map, job_events):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"acceptance file {job_real!r} is not in canonical "
                    "compact form")
            history, _supply_map, _supply_events, supply_raw = \
                _resources._load_file(supply_real)
            if supply_raw is None:
                raise FileNotFoundError(
                    f"supply file {supply_real!r} does not exist")
            signal_history, _signal_map, _signal_events, signal_raw = \
                _signals._load_file(signal_real)
            if signal_raw is None:
                raise FileNotFoundError(
                    f"signal file {signal_real!r} does not exist")
            # The ledger now accepts live trades, each freezing the
            # signal version it priced on; static trades validate as
            # before.
            trades, idempotency, old_bytes = _load_clear_ledger(
                ledger_real, accepted, history, signal_history)

            job = accepted.get(job_id)
            if job is None:
                raise KeyError(job_id)

            binding = idempotency.get(key)
            if binding is not None:
                if binding["job_id"] != job_id or binding["at"] != at:
                    raise ValueError("idempotency key was already used with "
                                     "a different request")
                return copy.deepcopy(trades[job_id]), False
            if job_id in trades:
                raise ValueError("job is already traded under another "
                                 "idempotency key")

            # Capacity already sold per exact resource version counts
            # every trade -- static and live alike -- so either clearing
            # path can oversell, and bookings never cross versions.
            sold: dict[tuple[str, int], int] = {}
            for trade in trades.values():
                slot = (trade["resource_id"], trade["version"])
                sold[slot] = sold.get(slot, 0) + trade["work"]

            residency = set(job["residency"])

                    (active["resource_id"], active["version"]), 0)

                    continue
                if active["end"] < job["deadline"]:
                    continue

                # one the resource is simply not a live candidate.
                signal = None

                            <= signal_record["expires"]:

                total_carbon = work * signal["carbon_intensity"]

                        or total_carbon > job["carbon_cap"]:
                    continue

                signal_copy["mix"] = dict(signal["mix"])
                candidates.append({
                    "resource": dict(active),
                    "signal": signal_copy,
                    "total_cost": total_cost,
                    "total_carbon": total_carbon,
                })

                entry["signal"]["carbon_intensity"],
                entry["signal"]["unit_cost"],
                entry["resource"]["resource_id"]))
            if not candidates:
                raise LookupError("no remaining feasible resource for job")

            winner = candidates[0]["resource"]
            resource_id = winner["resource_id"]
            version = winner["version"]
            trade: dict[str, Any] = {
                "job_id": job_id,
                "at": at,
                "work": work,
                "resource_id": resource_id,
                "version": version,
                "candidates": candidates,
                "selection": {"resource_id": resource_id,
                              "version": version},
            }
            trades[job_id] = trade
            idempotency[key] = {"job_id": job_id, "at": at}
            _commit_clear(ledger_real,
                          _canonical_clear_bytes(trades, idempotency),
                          old_bytes)

1	"""Persistent re-evaluation and migration advice for booked trades.
2	
3	The market already books a job against one exact resource version
4	(``market.clear``/``market.clear_live``), dispatch commits and claims
5	that decision and the execution layer runs launch or migration plans,
6	while the live signal ledger keeps publishing fresh region observations.
7	What is missing until this module is a re-evaluation of an unfinished
8	booking: given the signals valid *now*, should the job stay on the
9	resource version its trade froze, or migrate to another resource whose
10	current version is cleaner or cheaper right now?
11	
12	The module exposes two public calls. :func:`evaluate` reads the seven
13	layers -- the ``jobs.submit`` acceptance file, the resource supply file,
14	the live signal file, the ``market.clear`` clearing ledger, the dispatch
15	ledger, the execution ledger and this module's advice ledger -- as one
16	snapshot under their shared locks together with the advice ledger's
17	exclusive lock, all seven taken in resolved real-path order, so
18	concurrent calls across processes can never deadlock.
19	
20	The re-evaluation rules are deliberately asymmetric between the slot
21	the job already occupies and every alternative:
22	
23	* the retained item always uses the exact resource version the trade
24	  froze, even once that version's own supply window has closed -- the
25	  job is already running on it;
26	* a migration item uses only another resource's highest version valid
27	  at the evaluation moment, never another version of the same resource;
28	* every item prices on the region's latest signal observed no later
29	  than the moment and not expired at it, and keeps the job's region,
30	  residency, deadline, cost and carbon budgets;
31	* capacity is deducted per exact resource version from every trade
32	  other jobs booked, while this job's own frozen occupancy is never
33	  deducted twice.
34	
35	Feasible items are ordered by signal carbon intensity, then signal unit
36	cost, then resource id. When the first item is still the traded version
37	the advice is ``keep``; otherwise it is ``migrate`` to that first item.
38	
39	Advice is refused while the booking is past re-evaluation: a succeeded
40	dispatch decision or a completed execution plan raises ``ValueError``,
41	an active execution plan raises ``PermissionError`` and an evaluation
42	moment past the job deadline raises ``TimeoutError`` -- in that order,
43	and none of them writes advice. An unknown job or dispatch decision
44	raises ``KeyError`` and a job without a trade, or one with no feasible
45	item, raises ``LookupError``; neither creates the ledger.
46	
47	:func:`apply` turns one ``migrate`` advice into a persisted
48	re-reservation. It reads the same seven layers as one consistent
49	snapshot -- the seven inputs under shared locks, this time including
50	the advice ledger, and the intent ledger under its exclusive lock, all
51	eight taken in resolved real-path order -- and recomputes the candidate
52	set at the reservation moment under the same region, residency, budget,
53	deadline and ordering rules, deducting capacity per exact resource
54	version for every trade and every other job's intent while never
55	deducting this job's own source occupancy against itself. The advice
56	target must still be the first feasible candidate: a changed target, an
57	empty feasible set or insufficient remaining capacity raises
58	``LookupError`` and reserves nothing. Only an unfinished, unclaimed
59	booking may be re-reserved: a succeeded dispatch decision or a
60	completed execution plan raises ``ValueError``, a claimed decision or
61	an active plan raises ``PermissionError`` and a reservation moment past
62	the job deadline raises ``TimeoutError`` -- none of them writes. A
63	successful call freezes the job, the advice key, the moment, the source
64	and target selections, the target's supply and signal records, the
65	dispatch and execution states and the ``reserved`` state into the
66	intent ledger.
67	
68	The advice ledger (version 1) holds ``records`` keyed by idempotency
69	key and one ``audit`` event per first-served key; both sections are
70	ordered by key code point. A first evaluation returns
71	``(record, True)``; replaying the same key with the same job and
72	evaluation moment returns the stored record with ``False`` without
73	writing, while the same key with a changed request raises
74	``ValueError``.
75	
76	The intent ledger (version 1) holds ``intents`` keyed by job id and
77	ordered by job id code point, ``idempotency`` bindings ordered by key
78	code point and one ``audit`` event per first-served key binding the
79	complete request and the committed intent. A first reservation returns
80	``(record, True)``; replaying the same key with the same job, advice
81	key and moment returns the stored record with ``False`` without
82	writing, while the same key with a changed request, or a job already
83	reserved under another key, raises ``ValueError``.
84	
85	:func:`start`, :func:`record` and :func:`recover` close the migration
86	loop over the reserved intents. :func:`start` claims one intent that is
87	still ``reserved`` -- neither finished nor occupied -- and freezes the
88	intent's source and target resource versions into a migration plan
89	bound to an owner and a lease end that must not pass the job deadline;
90	the target capacity stays exclusively held by the intent for the whole
91	execution. :func:`record` lets the current owner, inside the lease,
92	commit the non-empty receipt of the next pending step -- ``copy`` then
93	``switch``, never skipped or repeated: a successful ``switch`` turns
94	the plan ``migrated`` and releases the source capacity the trade froze,
95	while any ``failed`` step turns it ``failed`` and releases the target
96	reservation immediately, leaving the source trade occupancy untouched.
97	:func:`recover` turns an active plan whose lease has strictly expired
98	into ``interrupted``, preserving every receipt and releasing the target
99	reservation. Capacity accounting recognizes the plan states: a
100	``reserved`` or ``active`` intent occupies both source and target, a
101	``migrated`` one only the target, a ``failed`` or ``interrupted`` one
102	only the source.
103	
104	The three calls share one idempotency key space with :func:`apply`:
105	replaying a key with the same request returns the current plan snapshot
106	with ``False`` and writes nothing, while the same key with a changed
107	request raises ``ValueError``. The first lifecycle action atomically

"""Persistent re-evaluation and migration advice for booked trades.

The market already books a job against one exact resource version
(``market.clear``/``market.clear_live``), dispatch commits and claims
that decision and the execution layer runs launch or migration plans,
while the live signal ledger keeps publishing fresh region observations.
What is missing until this module is a re-evaluation of an unfinished
booking: given the signals valid *now*, should the job stay on the
resource version its trade froze, or migrate to another resource whose
current version is cleaner or cheaper right now?

The module exposes two public calls. :func:`evaluate` reads the seven
layers -- the ``jobs.submit`` acceptance file, the resource supply file,
the live signal file, the ``market.clear`` clearing ledger, the dispatch
ledger, the execution ledger and this module's advice ledger -- as one
snapshot under their shared locks together with the advice ledger's
exclusive lock, all seven taken in resolved real-path order, so
concurrent calls across processes can never deadlock.

The re-evaluation rules are deliberately asymmetric between the slot
the job already occupies and every alternative:

* the retained item always uses the exact resource version the trade
  froze, even once that version's own supply window has closed -- the
  job is already running on it;
* a migration item uses only another resource's highest version valid
  at the evaluation moment, never another version of the same resource;
* every item prices on the region's latest signal observed no later
  than the moment and not expired at it, and keeps the job's region,
  residency, deadline, cost and carbon budgets;
* capacity is deducted per exact resource version from every trade
  other jobs booked, while this job's own frozen occupancy is never
  deducted twice.

Feasible items are ordered by signal carbon intensity, then signal unit
cost, then resource id. When the first item is still the traded version
the advice is ``keep``; otherwise it is ``migrate`` to that first item.

Advice is refused while the booking is past re-evaluation: a succeeded
dispatch decision or a completed execution plan raises ``ValueError``,
an active execution plan raises ``PermissionError`` and an evaluation
moment past the job deadline raises ``TimeoutError`` -- in that order,
and none of them writes advice. An unknown job or dispatch decision
raises ``KeyError`` and a job without a trade, or one with no feasible
item, raises ``LookupError``; neither creates the ledger.

:func:`apply` turns one ``migrate`` advice into a persisted
re-reservation. It reads the same seven layers as one consistent
snapshot -- the seven inputs under shared locks, this time including
the advice ledger, and the intent ledger under its exclusive lock, all
eight taken in resolved real-path order -- and recomputes the candidate
set at the reservation moment under the same region, residency, budget,
deadline and ordering rules, deducting capacity per exact resource
version for every trade and every other job's intent while never
deducting this job's own source occupancy against itself. The advice
target must still be the first feasible candidate: a changed target, an
empty feasible set or insufficient remaining capacity raises
``LookupError`` and reserves nothing. Only an unfinished, unclaimed
booking may be re-reserved: a succeeded dispatch decision or a
completed execution plan raises ``ValueError``, a claimed decision or
an active plan raises ``PermissionError`` and a reservation moment past
the job deadline raises ``TimeoutError`` -- none of them writes. A
successful call freezes the job, the advice key, the moment, the source
and target selections, the target's supply and signal records, the
dispatch and execution states and the ``reserved`` state into the
intent ledger.

The advice ledger (version 1) holds ``records`` keyed by idempotency
key and one ``audit`` event per first-served key; both sections are
ordered by key code point. A first evaluation returns
``(record, True)``; replaying the same key with the same job and
evaluation moment returns the stored record with ``False`` without
writing, while the same key with a changed request raises
``ValueError``.

The intent ledger (version 1) holds ``intents`` keyed by job id and
ordered by job id code point, ``idempotency`` bindings ordered by key
code point and one ``audit`` event per first-served key binding the
complete request and the committed intent. A first reservation returns
``(record, True)``; replaying the same key with the same job, advice
key and moment returns the stored record with ``False`` without
writing, while the same key with a changed request, or a job already
reserved under another key, raises ``ValueError``.

:func:`start`, :func:`record` and :func:`recover` close the migration
loop over the reserved intents. :func:`start` claims one intent that is
still ``reserved`` -- neither finished nor occupied -- and freezes the
intent's source and target resource versions into a migration plan
bound to an owner and a lease end that must not pass the job deadline;
the target capacity stays exclusively held by the intent for the whole
execution. :func:`record` lets the current owner, inside the lease,
commit the non-empty receipt of the next pending step -- ``copy`` then
``switch``, never skipped or repeated: a successful ``switch`` turns
the plan ``migrated`` and releases the source capacity the trade froze,
while any ``failed`` step turns it ``failed`` and releases the target
reservation immediately, leaving the source trade occupancy untouched.
:func:`recover` turns an active plan whose lease has strictly expired
into ``interrupted``, preserving every receipt and releasing the target
reservation. Capacity accounting recognizes the plan states: a
``reserved`` or ``active`` intent occupies both source and target, a
``migrated`` one only the target, a ``failed`` or ``interrupted`` one
only the source.

The three calls share one idempotency key space with :func:`apply`:
replaying a key with the same request returns the current plan snapshot
with ``False`` and writes nothing, while the same key with a changed
request raises ``ValueError``. The first lifecycle action atomically
upgrades the ledger to its history layout, keeping every recorded
intent, binding, receipt and audit event: intents are keyed by their
reservation (apply) key, plans by their own start key, the start request
persistently names its reserved intent and each step/recovery request
names its plan. Only the first change of a call commits the plan, its
state, the idempotency binding and the audit event atomically. Every read requires the on-disk bytes to be exactly the
canonical compact form :func:`_canonical_bytes` produces -- compact
UTF-8 JSON with non-ASCII written through, no negative-zero or
non-finite number literals and exactly one trailing newline -- and
every commit goes through a synced same-directory temporary file, an
atomic replace and a directory fsync, restoring the pre-call bytes on
failure, so an unsuccessful call leaves neither a temporary fragment
nor half an audit event.

:func:`settle` finally gives later dispatch and execution a current
occupancy that survives the terminal plan, without rewriting any of
the existing layers: it writes one independent settlement ledger
(loaded read-only by :func:`current`). A ``migrated`` plan confirms the
target version as the current binding and retires the source version
as the previous-generation binding; a ``failed`` or ``interrupted``
plan compensates with the current occupancy kept on the source
version. Migrations are no longer limited to one per job: the intent
ledger keeps every reservation (keyed by its apply key) and every plan
(keyed by its own start key), and each terminal plan settles exactly
once into the job's continuous generation chain -- the immutable trade
is generation 0, the first settlement generation 1, and every later
settlement chains from the binding the previous completed settlement
left behind. A new round of advice, reservation or migration is rooted
at the latest completed binding, so it never falls back to the original
trade, while a settlement still in ``pending`` is not a generation and
blocks both another settlement and a follow-up migration. Each
settlement lands through a crash-safe two-phase commit
-- a durable ``pending`` record, binding and audit event first, then
the advance to ``active`` or ``compensated`` -- so a crash between the
two writes is resumed by the same key carrying the same request, which
completes the missing stage and still returns ``True``; only an
already completed same-key request returns the record with ``False``
without writing a byte.
"""

    jobs: str,
    supply: str,
    signals: str,
    trades: str,
    dispatch: str,
    execution: str,
    ledger: str,
    job_id: str,
    key: str,
    at: int,

    files are read as one snapshot under their shared locks together

    the call raises ``LookupError`` without writing.

    execution states, the ordered candidates, the recommendation

    ``migrate``) and the target selection. A missing advice ledger is
    created only by the first record, the record and its audit event

            # flight exactly like an active execution plan.

                plan["job_id"] == job_id and plan["state"] == "active"

                        or total_carbon > job["carbon_cap"]:

                    "resource": dict(resource_record),
                    "signal": signal,
                    "total_cost": total_cost,
                    "total_carbon": total_carbon,

                                 "resource version")

            # valid at the moment -- never another version of the current

                    continue

                    if version_record["start"] <= at <= version_record["end"]:
                        active = version_record
                if active is None:
                    continue
                consider(active)

            candidates.sort(key=lambda entry: (
                entry["signal"]["carbon_intensity"],
                entry["signal"]["unit_cost"],
                entry["resource"]["resource_id"]))

                raise LookupError("no feasible resource for the job at "
                                  "the evaluation moment")

            winner = candidates[0]["resource"]
            target = {"resource_id": winner["resource_id"],
                      "version": winner["version"]}
            recommendation = ("keep" if target == current else "migrate")
            if job_plans:
                execution_state = max(
                    job_plans.values(),
                    key=lambda plan: plan["attempt"])["state"]

                execution_state = "none"

                "job_id": job_id,
                "at": at,
                "current": current,
                "dispatch": decision["state"],
                "execution": execution_state,
                "candidates": candidates,
                "recommendation": recommendation,
                "target": target,
            }

            events[key] = {"key": key, "request": dict(request),
                           "result": copy.deepcopy(record)}
            _commit_file(ledger_real,
                         _canonical_bytes(records, events), old_bytes)
            return copy.deepcopy(record), True
